title: Showstopper!
text:
I love red and when Fashion Land offered to let me test out this scarf I jumped at the chance to wear this beautiful fashion accessory. The red color and the design is what drew me to it. It is a show stopper.

When I opened the box I was struck by the beautiful presentation. The scarf is in a lovely red box. Inside there’s an added surprise of a Chinese Knot and a gift box for it. I’ve used these before to hang off dresser pulls, doors and you can even put them on a Christmas tree. Many uses for them. The scarf is wrapped in tissue. Also included is a pretty red gift bag.

The scarf is 100% silk and is very soft and supple. I loved the feel of it. It is super long. I can wrap this several times around my neck. A brochure is enclosed to show you different ways to wear the scarf. It is also unisex so men and women can wear it.

Instructions say to dry clean or wash by hand. Use a medium temperature iron. As far as I can tell it looks well made.

This is a beautiful accessory that you’d be proud to wear out to dinner, to the theater or any event. FYI: In my photo I didn't try to style the scarf. I wanted to let you see the beautiful design and length.

I received this free for my unbiased and honest opinion.

FYI: Modern Usage of Artistic Knots

Along with being symbolic gifts or messages, knots are still used if they wear traditional Chinese clothing or as good luck charms. They are a means of fastening traditional garments instead of buttons or wooden pegs. Now, silk is most widely used to make these clothing knots.
They are used as jewelry such as even rings, earrings, bracelets, and necklaces. They are sold as handicraft novelty items too.

This is a pretty cool toy, but the quality sucks. I bought it to use for a game of a dance-style game of hot-potato at my nephew's Fortnite birthday party. Unfortunately it broke immediately after opening so we weren't able to use it that way.

As noted by other reviewers, the whole thing is plastic except the chain, which is totally fine for the body and maybe even the pin itself, but the ring on the pin should absolutely not be plastic as kids need to yank on it to pull the pin out. I pulled it once and it was fine, but a kid pulled it two times and it snapped in half.

What I should have done was brought a metal keyring with me to replace the plastic ring, but I didn't think ahead to do that. What the makers should do is replace the ring with a metal ring... It would be a super cool toy if they would make that minor change.

I have seen reviews that list watch movements getting slow or non-functioning within days of purchase, this is because the BATTERY is old and needs to be replaced in my experience, not because the watches movement isn't working.

The wristband is two piece vinyl construction that is comfortable on your wrist. However, I did not like the white stitching which looked very tacky. I had some problems with the watch band buckle adjustment, the end of the strap broke and the buckle came loose. The wristband is constructed with thin strips of vinyl over foam rubber. title: To Be Or Not To Be, That Is The Question.. Leather, That Is..
text:
Do you have any idea how many times we have purchased belts in this family that promised that they were leather, only to have them crack or fall apart rather quickly? Of course you don't! But let me give you a hint- TOO MANY! Let's take a look at this belt.

WHAT IS THIS BELT LIKE?
This belt is supposed to be 100% full grain leather. It comes rolled up in a satin bag with a draw string. The belt itself has a plastic rubbery coating on it front and back and edges to make it black. The surface is satin in nature- not matte and not shiny. The smell, however, is definitely chemical- plastic type smell.

QUALITY
The belt looks nice, but the edges when wearing already are showing signs of abrasions on the edges as they hit the belt loops. I am wondering how long before the inside is showing and we will know if it is indeed a solid piece of leather or a bonded type leather.

BUCKLE
The buckle is a a nice antiqued pewter type color. It is a heavy buckle and really designer looking.

PACKAGING
This packaging is a satin bag with a drawstring, appropriate for gift giving.

SIZE?
The belt I got was a size 36.

IS IT REALLY LEATHER?
Only time will tell if this is really solid leather. I have been burned so many times in the past, that I tend to wait and see. Hopefully this really is a solid piece of leather and won't crack or fall apart quickly.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a belt that is casual or dressy, fits with a wide variety of clothing styles and can be worn by men or women, depending on the style it is worn with, this is a nice choice. It seems like leather, but the coating has me concerned with how fast it is going to scrape and wear off.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I prefer all natural full grain leather belts to be stained and left natural. This belt is okay, but time will tell how long before it starts to look ragged.

I then ordered this lace-up style due to new job requirements. I wanted to try Orthofeet's insole but found that made the shoe too tight so I took it out and put in my custom orthotic along with the thicker spacer and got a nice snug fit. I wear these shoes with a light support knee-high and the fit is great. After just wearing the shoes for a short time, I felt the relief of my feet not hurting at all. I am going to be doing a LOT more walking with my job and I was worried about being able to do that without being in agony. These shoes fit the bill. title: Sporty, Yes. Sensitive skin, No.
text:
I really like this type of stretchy, sporty band for my Fitbit. I've used something similar to this with my Versa 2 for a couple of years and love it. I recently upgraded to a Versa 4, so I ordered these bands to wear with it. They are nice and stretchy, adjustable, and should fit any size wrist.

BUT.... the material of these bands is different than what I've been using, and that is not a good thing. These bands irritate my skin, and I find myself taking off the Fitbit from time to time just to get relief from it. That is not because the band is on too tight. There is something in the fabric that irritates my skin. Nylon? My skin is sensitive, I must use latex free bandages in order to avoid a rash, and I'm careful about any moisturizer I put on my face. I have also had issues with the band that typically comes with the Fitbitd devices, part of the reason I order different bands.

With the Versa 4 I actually find the Fitbit band that comes with it to be more comfortable than this stretchy band. I definitely would not order these again.

title: Cheap softshell fabric, overall fairly well made, light to medium weight. Zipper is in backward.
text:
Approximate measurements: Black size Medium
Chest: underarm to underarm 24"
Length: front shoulder to hem 27", back top of collar to hem 30.5"
Shoulders: across back sleeve seam to seam 19.5"
Sleeve length: underarm to cuff 19.5", shoulder seam to cuff 25.5"
Waist: across banded hem side to side unstretched 18"

My husband wears size large in basic t-shirts, fruit of the loom, Haynes etc, and the medium jacket fit well. Loose enough for easy movement but not so baggy that it looked oversized. It's a light-medium weight jacket, more than a windbreaker but less than a medium weight. The softshell outer fabric is a cheap version and more like a water repellant polyester or nylon style. I think the softshell fabric has a thin lining/backing between the actual lining because it has an almost 'puffy' feel to it. Due to the style and fit it's definitely a men's jacket but like other reviewers have noted, the zipper is backward so it zips like a woman's jacket. It came out of the plastic packet with a chemical smell which I'm hoping will go away after washing. Overall it appears to be a cheaply but fairly well made jacket which will be good for fall and possibly early mild winter with a sweater. I rated in 3 stars, it lost stars due to the cheap style softshell, backward zipper and would have looked better with basic black or grey lining.

I have a drawer full of head wraps and I wear every single one of them. I know these are called "headbands" but it is programmed in my head to call them head wraps ;). I am a runner and hiker and I simply will not, and cannot, go without a head wrap. They are so completely versatile it is hard for me to understand why I do not see everyone else wear them. Ha! I wear them in so many ways and for so many things: as a headband, ear warmers, over my nose and mouth as a dust guard, cover the back of my neck so I do not get a sun burn, for bikram yoga and spin to help keep sweat from pouring into my eyes. Not to mention it also keeps my hair out of my eyes.

Not every head wrap is created equal. I prefer the thinner and softer material that also has a little bit of stretch. I was afforded the opportunity to get one discounted for me to share what I think. I did not bat one eye. It is a head wrap! Of course! When I took it out of its package I noticed right away the material is very soft and silky feeling. It has a some stretch to it which makes it nice to work with when you are stretching it over your head, twisting and tucking it behind your head…etc. It is lightweight so my head feels like it can breathe. I live in AZ and anything that traps heat in while running in the summer is a big ‘no’. I got the Dia de los Muertos design and I love it. I did get another wrap in a different design, so I will be leaving the same feedback for that one, as well. Two thumbs up for these bands!

title: Not bad but could be SO MUCH BETTER!
text:
Sizing runs more towards Asian sizing rather than us. The 5x probably equates to a 20 or 22 US size.

This skirt is not nearly as flared as the image would lead you to believe. The plating is relatively flat with only two or three plates that naturally occur around the same lines. It is not nearly as pleated as the image shows. Once you line with a crinoline or a petticoat, the pleating will be even less.

Some of the stitching does not quite line up. For example, in the bodice where the bow shape is, the center of the bow does not line up with the center of the point of the bodice insert. It was probably done to align the floral image, but it twists the bodice a bit.

The fabric is quite stretchy, but wrinkles very easily. The dress came packaged in a bag, much like a men's dress shirt. It will definitely need to be cleaned - washed and dried - before you can wear it. You will surely have to iron it afterwards as well.

Returning to the sewing, some of the seams seem a little loose and less than perfectly sewn. Workmanship is not great but maybe good at best. This is probably something you only be able to wear a few times, probably not much more than a dozen. I do not foresee the workmanship keeping this dress together for more than a handful of waring's.

title: Feeling very let down on this purchase
text:
Feeling very let down on this purchase.

This was the 2nd case that I have purchased from these folks.

Previous History: The first purchase I ever made from them was for a set of their readers. I gave them a 5 star review praising them.

The second purchase was for another set of their readers in case they ever went out of business. That's how much I liked their product! Their readers are definitely the best I have ever purchased in over 25 years of using them. I just told my wife a couple of days ago that I'll probably need more powerful lenses before these glasses die.

After receiving the first set of readers, I ordered a case to protect them. The case (1st time ordering one) was absolutely perfect in fit and finish, literally. I was once again very impressed by their workmanship and quality control. Another 5 star review from me.

Then I received the second case that I ordered a few days ago. I had really thought that this outfit was the epitome of quality construction before I received this case.

Unfortunately, the top and bottom pieces don’t seat properly. This should have certainly been noticed before it was sent out the door.

I played with it for a while and it looks better. However, since I was squeezing it and forcing it out of its initial fit, I’m sure it won’t stay this way forever.

I was very disappointed in this particular item. I see that it is reverting back to its previous fit after only 24 hours or so. Since it looks somewhat better now (temporarily) I can’t be bothered returning it. I just feel let down.

I will still order readers from them when the time comes, but only one set at a time.

P.S. I HAD to select "Fit as expected" since the top and bottom are the correct sizes, they just don't fit together.

title: Performed Well
text:
I bought this specifically to take along as I hiked the Camino de Santiago in northern Spain. Although it added weight to my pack, it performed well on the three days I had to use it. The length kept me dry to about mid-calf on my 5'6" frame. It's generously cut so that I could carry a day pack underneath without losing any significant coverage, as well as wear warm layers for the 45-degree temperatures. The drawstring on the hood helped keep it in place in winds that were high enough to make me stagger. The sleeves were long enough so that I could pull my gloved hands back inside and grip my hiking poles through the plastic. With snaps on the sleeves, the jacket, and the pockets, no rain was able to get in. The one drawback is that this jacket doesn't breathe, so any sweat wasn't able to evaporate. Having anticipated this, I had worn layers that stayed warm even when damp.
Overall, this inexpensive jacket did what I needed it to do in some pretty miserable conditions. I don't think it was the best choice for a 500-mile hike because of the weight and bulk, but I was grateful to have it. I plan to keep in it in my travel trailer from now on. It will fit just about anyone, and it will be useful for those unavoidable trips outside on rainy days.

title: Affordable, nice quality polarized sunglasses
text:
I bought these when they were a lighting deal for $10 and, for the price, I am very satisfied with them. The lenses are pretty big--a little bigger than I prefer, but that is my personal preference and not a fault with the product. The glasses fit comfortably on my average sized head and the huge lenses definitely do a good job of shielding my eyes from the intense Texas sun.

Pros:
-very affordable
-metal hinges that should hold up much better than plastic ones
-are polarized as advertised
-look nice
-comfortable
-comes with a sturdy, zippered case that has a clip to attach to a bag or belt loop. The case is actually fairly compact and light. Also comes with cloth wipe and glasses screwdriver keychain.
-the bling on the frame does not have the metal claps holding them in (they use some sort of white adhesive instead) which means it does not get painfully caught in hair

Cons:
-if you want a very lightweight pair of glasses, these are a little on the heavier side because of the metal on the frame
-if you have a small face, these lenses may overwhelm your face because they are very large.
- because they used a white adhesive, the bling looks a little sloppy up close (however, their listing images show the same thing, so it should not come as a surprise). Not a big issue, just something to be aware of if that would bother you.

(UPDATE) After wearing these socks for maybe six times they have already developed a large have hole in the heel. Pretty much making these garbage. I am going to try to make some calf sleeves out of these since I never really cared about the foot portion anyways. The compression is the best out of anything I have tried, so I think they will serve as good sleeves. But there is no way I can recommend these shocks now.

These socks are awesome, I surprised by how well they fit and the quality of the construction. These socks have a lot of compression around the leg and calf area, which I really like. It is a tight knit weave that looks to be very durable. This tight knit weave continues down over the top of the foot, but underneath is a softer more padded construction. To me this makes the socks much more comfortable, as they are not compression the foot all the time. The toe area is a thinner lighter material, I like this, it allows the toes to breathe and wiggle around. The only thing I don’t like is that the seam that switches material here at the toes is not done very well. I am not sure if it because of where it is at or if it is just a poor quality seem, but I can feel the shoe pressing up against it and then it pressing up against my feet. I kind of got used to it after a while and mostly forgot about it. Other than this small complaint these are great socks, I would highly recommend them. title: Great belt. Just be careful showing it off.
text:
I've had this belt for about a week, and so far, I love it! I have very, VERY minor issues with it, which I'll cover first. But its so minor it doesn't make for any lack of stars. Overall great belt, and I'm going to be buying different styles VERY soon.

First: I can't believe I'm going to say this about a belt...but...it has a learning curve. I know: "haha, dude can't use a belt!". But you get so used to the "hunk of fabric with holes" belt system, any change kind of upsets a system of putting pants on. I like having my belt tight to keep my pants up, shirt tucked it, and my slew of belt attachments in place. Trying to get this belt nice and tight requires a bit of a suck in of the gut, and some pulling (but nothing the average John or Jill couldn't do) to get it nice and tight.

Another small issue is the belt size itself. The belt was much, MUCH longer then I though. I bought 4 inchs over my waist, to ensure I had enough play to do what I need to get the belt secure. I'm so used to buying cheap Wal-Mart belts that I tend to always over shoot my waist size to ensure I have enough, and that I can salvage the belt a bit when it finally starts to go. I feel like it should have outlined how the belt size works a bit more clearly, but I know I'm the idiot here, so it's nothing against the belt! Even more so, the belts are cheap, and I can easily get a smaller one if I want.

Those two small issues aside, though, this thing is great! The belt itself is a nice, solid material that don't fold or twist easily when trying to put the thing on. The buckle is sturdy, simple, and works exactly like it should. Even better is that is not nickle, so I don't have to worry about my minor nickle allergy like I used to with old belts.

Either way, like I said at the start. Great belt. A bit more then I normal spend on belts, but worth every penny. I keep showing it off because of how well it works! Which, in hindsight, saying "Look what I got!" and reaching for my pants may not be the best way to get people interested in an awesome belt...

title: My first and only G-Shock
text: Normally a sports/dive watch kind of guy. I do, however , like the idea of an "indestructible", anti-magnetic tool watch. I bought this as a work beater. From my understanding, this is a blacked-out out version of the G-100, and I think, better looking. So far, I like it. My only complaint was that when I received the watch. It was losing seconds. I reluctantly  changed the battery, instead of sending it back. Still on the fence about G-Shocks in general. My opinion is that it really isn't as hard to set as some people have said. the analog time is sync with the digital time. The minute hand moves with the digital time every 20 seconds. Once you get the hands in the correct position, it's set. I would have liked for the hands to have better lume. For this I have to take away a star. My way around this, is to hit mode to put it on the digital time and in the middle of the night, I can just push the light button. My ideal setup is analog time on the face and the digital display to have day/date. Good watch, but you're paying a little bit of a premium for the blacked-out utilitarian look. ***UPDATE*** After 2 years of ownership, it's still going. The watch is still losing time. This is not something I'm used to with regular quartz analog watches I've owned, as they typically run fast.  The "module" loses at least 5 sec/month on avg. I'm now on my 3rd CR2016 battery. I use the timer on a daily basis and become reliant on the features. When you take the watch from hot to cold a sm. amount of fog becomes visible on the face, then goes away. Next battery change I plan to make sure I'm in the driest environment possible and will use a bit of liquid silicone on the seal. I believe that the watch is watertight. After 2 years, it's a bit battered and abused, but still earning its keep.

title: Screen touch excellent but not very warm

The good:
Screen touch is great. The best I’ve tried yet. It’s as good as touch with uncovered fingers. This is very useful if, like me, you need to use your phone for navigation or other purposes in the backcountry, regardless of the season or weather.

The less good:
Not super warm. They’re good to around 40F, but in colder temps your fingers will probably get cold. Adding flip back mittens over them in temps below 25F works.
My only other wish is that the wrist elastic was wider and tighter as the gloves tend to slide down if not tucked under a jacket cuff. It’s an annoying kerfuffel if you have to remove a glove and put it on again.

text: The MP3 player is easy to hook up and works well.  It plays MP3s from a micro SD card or a USB drive or both.  I found that it will automatically play whichever is plugged in. The volume on the headphone jack was much lower.  The headphone jack will work for headphones but won't drive a speaker without external amplification.  At high volume there is some noticeable white noise.  The only drawback I found is that it is mono not stereo.  It has volume buttons (long press) and previous and next track buttons (short press).  It doesn't have skip forward and back buttons which I find a requirement for listening to audio books or podcasts.  It has a repeat track mode button and play/pause. title: Very comfy, and nicely padded on the bottom. A little thin on top around ankle.
text:
Most importantly, these socks a SUPER comfortable, and I am looking forward to seeing how they perform for actual hiking---but I have no concerns. The bottoms of your feet will feet nice and cushy, as that is where these socks are thickest. They are thinner around the tops of your feet---particularly the ankle area. As these are 100% wool, I think that is probably by design so you're less likely to overheat your feet and it's lighter on the material for the most-flexed area.

That said, because of the weave and the stretch there, I am a little concerned about how well they will hold up in these thinner areas. (You can see your skin a little between the stitching). It's obvious this is by design, as there are definitive lines to how different areas of the socks are stitched.

So, basically, just be careful when putting them on to keep this area from getting stretched out. Don't do a lot of hard tugging at the top of the socks and you should be fine. It isn't a high-wear area, so it isn't likely to wear out so much as get pulled out.

title: Love this dress, but can't lift my arms
text: These dresses are beautiful. I bought one a year or so ago (the Multicolour 2). The sizing seemed a little wonky. So, instead of ordering a small, as I usually do, I sized up and got a large. It fit very well. I've worn that dress a ton, and always get a lot of compliments on it. It's very comfortable, light-weight, flowy, and the fabric is not restrictive in anyway. I most recently purchased the "Green" (dark green with red and white flowers). I debated about the sizing because this dress has a different size chart than the Multicolour 2. After reviewing the chart, I ended up choosing a small. It fits like a glove - IF I don't lift my arms at all. The chest, waist, and length are great, but the sleeves of this particular dress are sewn in a way where the fabric has no give. Additionally, it is a different, thicker material than the first dress I ordered, where I had no movement limitations. It breaks my heart because the dress LOOKS like it fits perfectly, and the print is stunning in-person, but I don't think I can wear it comfortably (at some point, I may have to lift my arms, ha). I just ordered a different dress (which I think is the same sizing as the original Multicolour 2), so I'm going to see if that works better. If not, I'll try to order the Green in a size up. All in all, when you find the right size, they are gorgeous, multi-functional dresses. I've worn my old one to the beach, for casual hang-outs, and to weddings. You may have to be patient with the sizing, or order a couple or different sizes, and return the one that doesn't fit.

title: Great little device, but could use some improvements
text:
I like this small MP3 module - easy to use (manually) and the sound quality is decent.

I'd recommend some improvements:

1) Put some headers on the board so one can (easily) connect the buttons to external controllers - I had to solder wires to the ends of the tiny button connections so I could interface this with a NodeMCU (or Arduino) for my purposes. It was a pain in the butt, but I managed.

2) Ability to set boot options (that are stored/remembered for the next boot). The default on boot is that it starts playing the first .mp3 file on the card - that seems daft to me. The default should be no sound on boot, and that you trigger the playing of .mp3s by pressing the button - or at least have a way to toggle that (perhaps with a couple of header pins on the board).

3) Include some documentation with the board - there is none. There are locations to solder battery connections (BAT+ and BAT-) on the board - and one ASSUMES that, because the default power source is USB, that 5v is what's needed, the same could be said of other boards (e.g. some ESP8266) that are 3.3v and would be fried if you applied 5v to VCC.

4) It would also be great to be able to access the button functions via the micro-USB port programmatically - perhaps there is, but with no documentation, no one knows.

text:
I bought this bag because I love Baggallini and I have the Metro bag (similar to this) in leopard print. I wanted an alternative to switch up a bit. This bag looks cool in the picture but in person it is not what it seems. By the photo it looks like you can stuff this bag, after all it IS called "BIG EVERYDAY BAG"... not. By the time you put stuff in the zippered pockets, there is no room to put anything on the inside, let alone navigate to any stuff that you managed to fit in there. If you filled the change purse good luck fitting on the inside with the outer pockets full.

They really cheesed down the materials on this bag compared to the Metro bag. The strap is not as wide or durable feeling as on the Metro bag. The little rings that hold the strap on the bag are smaller as well. The included change purse doesn't have a side pocket. The top zipper is cheaper and more flimsy.

Trust me, I could not fit the entire contents of my Metro bag into this bag no matter how I arranged the stuff. And, my Metro bag still had a ton of room in it.

2 stars for looks but the storage is poorly designed.

Soft and warm.

It's a little big at the top; no one's head is that long.

Overall, this is a fantastic hat and at $20 (the price at the time of this review), it's a steal!

title: Our favorite, all-purpose shoe for busy little feet
text:
I love Pedipeds. From the Originals, which are far easier to put on squishy feet than Robeez, to the Pediped Flex for older toddlers/preschoolers, they are fantastic shoes for the little ones. Flex shoes are, as the name suggests, very flexible and yet supportive. Add in the cuteness factor and, well, you have a winner.

The Isabella shoe is our favorite. We loved the brown pair originally purchased so much that we bought another pair this year. They're neutral and suitable for any outfit; they're a cinch for young ones to get on and off by themselves; they're well-made and durable. I especially appreciate the removable inserts that allow the shoes to fit a bit more snugly in the early days when they might otherwise be too big to wear safely. They add quite a bit of wearable time to each size's lifespan.

The only downfall of this particular style is that the toes get fairly easily scuffed up in the course of preschooler play, but this is to be expected. (I take it as a reassuring sign that she's doing the things a preschooler should be doing!) It didn't stop us from buying a second pair, and I have every intention of grabbing another next year as well.

title: have a 33” waist (that’s all the better I can do after having 4 kids)
text:
I rely on detailed reviews when I purchase items off the internet. This product did have one anywhere! – Not even on the company’s website! So I purchased 2 sizes (after learning that I can return the product for free) to determine the fit. I am 5’6”, weight 132 pounds, have a 33” waist (that’s all the better I can do after having 4 kids), and have 37” hips. The sizing charts on all the pants/shirts products both on Amazon and the company’s website have very skinny waists. I bought a medium and a large. Both fit. The large, however, made my hips look too big. The way the skirt hangs makes the hips flair/stick out on the sides too much. So I stuck with the medium. I could probably get away with a small, but nothing is worse than having something too tight. So, when determining size with leggings/skirts, I personally would go with the hip measurements, not the waist measurement. The 28”/29” waist fit around my 33” waist no problem and it is not overly snug.

This skirt if very comfortable and the leggings can be adjusted to how long you want them. If you want it to look like you are just wearing a nice skirt, you can pull the leggings up to your knees . . . and it is still comfortable.

Since these are leggings, not loose shorts, there is no attached brief inside. You can wear your own underwear, wear nothing, or purchase an official swim brief (for fast drying purposes).

A couple things about the skirt that I did not know:
There are ties on the inside side of the skirt and the outside side of the leggings. These ties can be tied together when swimming to keep the skirt from floating up. When the ties are untied, the ties are short enough that they are not hanging down past the bottom of the skirt.

Cons:
While the elastic in the waistband is nice and wide, it seems to twist every time I put the skirt on. Every time I put it on I have to manipulate the elastic so that it lays flat in the casing. This is no big deal because I am going to put 2 or 3 small cross-stitches in the waist band to keep the elastic from twisting every time I take it off or put it on. Once it is on, the elastic doesn’t twist. And you can’t really tell too much from the outside when it is twisted because the elastic is loose inside the waist band, so the waist band still lies flat.
Also, it might just be how I am built, but there are a few wrinkles/puckers in the skirt between my waist and the top of my butt. The skirt is well built, in that it doesn’t look like that should happen, and it lies nice and flat everywhere else. Maybe my but sticks out too much? Or maybe the material wasn’t pulled up high enough in the waist band when they sewed it together? Anyway, I don’t think this is a big deal because I am wearing a swim shirt or tankini top that will cover it up (even when I raise my hands all the way up).

title: Excellent "first" FiveFingers!
text: Our whole family wears FiveFingers, so my husband and I were delighted to find these designed with the youngest wearers in mind.  Unlike other FiveFingers, the tongue has strong velcro strips running down both sides lengthwise.  This allows you to lift the entire tongue up and out of the shoe all the way down to the toe.  It's ideal for young kids who need help getting their toes into the shoe's "fingers."  I spread the shoe wide open, put my child's foot inside, then run my finger down each toe to make sure it's sitting in the right place.  The velcro makes this kind of access quick and easy.  The velcro itself is strong and sticks well.  We haven't had any problems with it popping open as my daughter walks.  The shoes stay on even when my daughter wears them on the gym's climbing wall.  Well worth the money to get your child started on the barefoot path.

I got many compliments from doctors, nurses and other patients and they wanted to know where I got it. After the surgery, I wore it over a tank top for a fun casual everyday look. It is listed under cover-ups but I think it could great for the office or to wear over a tank top just out and about on a warm summers day. The black floral pattern goes with a lot and it really attractive. This will fit a wide range of people, too. It has one single tie closure in the front if you need to keep it secure although it really does not close. It is flowy and has great movement. This black floral does not seem quite as see through as some of the lighter shades. I really like it and think it will be handy in the coming summer months.

title: It worked for what I needed it for
text:
I was surprised to learn just how hard it was to find a dress appropriate for a wedding. It took hitting store after store to find everything was either too casual or too fancy. Luckily I had come across this dress in my search and had kept it as an available option. Just a few days before I decided this would be the dress I wore to my friend's wedding. While not ideal, it definitely did the job.

I first ordered this dress in an XS. Given in most brands I'm a 0 or 2 (I'm 5'7" approx. 125-130), I thought an XS would be perfect. Wrong. It was SO snug up top (I'm not well-endowed in the least), I couldn't even zip the thing up. So, I next ordered a small with only a couple days to spare. Luckily I was able to zip this one up.

As for the style itself, it fit a little awkwardly. Like I mentioned it was quite snug in the chest/arm area (even having ordered a size up), while from the empire waist down it was EXTREMELY flowy. Like, almost maternity-like. It would have been nice if it was a little less large from the waist down.

Having said that, I did get a lot of compliments on the dress. It was the right length so it was easy to dance in, and it was appropriate for the occasion. I'd recommend this dress if you're in a pinch and need something for a similar occasion.

title: Exactly What I'd Been After
text:
These are great.

I will admit that, like others have said, there is an odor, but I can say from experience working with leather, that it is just the dye. There is nothing harmful nor toxic about it, it is to be expected from freshly dyed leather, and it is normal.

Now that that has been addressed, let's move on.

These fit just slightly large. I normally wear an 8.5-9, so I went with 9, and find them a bit roomy. I knew this was a risk, but because I was uncertain about the cushiness of the sole, I wanted to have the option for an insole. As it turns out, these are wicked comfy as is. I may need to add an arch support because of my particular foot needs, and I for sure have room to do so, which is great.

I have super long toes, and find the toe box extremely comfortable, and not pinched.

The leather is soft, and does not bite into my foot anywhere. Coupled with the softness of the sole rubber, I do not expect to have "breaking in" of these boot. A rarity. They have the added benefit of not being heavy because of the sole design and material.

I have a pet peeve about unnecessary zippers on boots. If the boot laces closed, there is no need for a zipper as far as I am concerned. I will rage about it. That behind said, this boot has a necessary zipper. The boot does not lace closed. The laces are to adjust the foot width and ankle snugness to your needs. Once that is done, you do not need to adjust them again, just use the zipper. Even with the laces at the loosest, these are not pull-on/slip-on boots. You need the zipper. The zipper is nice quality, and even has a slight curve to the pull to help it sit more flush while wearing the boot. A wonderful, easily overlooked detail, that I truly appreciate.

I love the design, the shape, the materials, the silhouette, and the fit. They look great on my feet, with my Jean's, and I will definitely wear them with skirts, too.

I expect that I will be ordering another pair in the near future because I love them that much. Tis a pity that I cannot give these more stars.

title: Weirdly Shaped
text:
I am 5'3", about 100 pounds, and usually wear a US XS or XXS, Asian S. This sweater is very short and wide, with very short sleeves.
I gave this sweater 3 tries. First, I ordered a SMALL. It was pretty baggy and loose, but the sleeves barely passed my elbows, and the bottom of the sweater barely reached my waist. I thought it was probably a dud--it happens. I decided to size up to a MEDIUM for the replacement because I wanted length like the picture and figured it couldn't really be too baggy. The sleeves on the medium still fell short of my wrists and the bottom hit above the waistband of my jeans.
I LOVE the fabric and the colors, so I decided to give it one more shot--I ordered an XL/EXTRA LARGE in a different color as I wanted baggy anyway, and the bigger size would get me the length I wanted. NOPE.
The sleeves in the XL barely touch my wrists with my arms at my side, but if I raise my arms, the sleeves are short. The bottom is still far shy of my hips--again, I'm only 5ft 3in--most everything is too long for me. The body fit the same as the small and medium, but the sleeves were ridiculously big, like lantern sleeves, which are nice, but not for this sweater.

So overall, a star because the knitting and colors are beautiful, but the fit is too weird to make it a wearable piece.

text:
I purchased mine on their website because they were running a discount code for black Friday and got 10 bucks off. Might be worth checking there for discount codes before trying to purchase here.

This is by far the best belt I've ever worn. It's so lightweight and gives just the right amount of tension around your waist. It sucks when you are between holes on regular belts and have to go tighter than needed just to keep your pants from falling down. With this one I get the perfect fit every time. It also looks amazing - I'm into really functional, clean looking design, and this ticks both boxes for me. So lightweight and so clean looking.

The only thing that might make me think twice about purchasing more is the price. I got mine for 25... I would say 35 bucks is OK the first time, but I could see this price keeping me away from buying additional colors. Don't get me wrong- their asking price as an introduction to the belt is well worth it- I just don't feel it's necessary to buy additional colors at this price to have around. One works just fine, so before you go spending 70 bucks to switch the colors around, give that a thought.

title: Great looking but not the best quality.
text:
For the price and brand name, I expected better quality. I took a risk buying an expensive pair of shoes for a growing teenager, but my son really loved them. Unfortunately, within 1 month the plastic in the heel stand on the back of the shoe got bent and was digging in to the back of my son's foot. We were able to fix the plastic with some muscle and determination, but six months later there are some sharp shards in that same area on both shoes that are stabbing my son. We haven't even owned these shoes for a year.
With the rigidity of the material used on the exterior of the heel, they could have used rubber or a more malleable support for the interior of the heel stand. The hard plastic that is in there feels like glass when it is cracked or bent. Poor design and quality since any stress to that portion of the shoe causes damage that make these unwearable.
Good looking shoes that are comfortable when they are not broken, but I wouldn't spend the money on this brand again.

I personally prefer that it is faux leather anyway, for ethical reasons, and just wanted to mention that here so nobody is disappointed thinking they are getting 5 animal leather pouches.

The swallow dress is a softer more stretchy cloth/cotton feeling type fabric (it's not cotton but I'm not sure how to better describe it), and the hem is an even length around the whole dress and skims the top of my feet. The black floral dress is more polyester/faux-silk feeling and the front of the hem line is higher and hits right below the knee while the back is at my feet. It also has a separate navy blue under layer while the swallow dress is just one layer. The difference in sizing is in how much fabric is in the bust area. There is more coverage available with the large. Honestly even with the large I'm going to wear a lace bralette undeenesth. The dress style is pretty low cutting regardless of size. Because the swallow dress is a stretchier fabric, you can adjust it in place to cover almost the same about. Long story short, I love how they both fit in all areas but the bust so I'm planning on keeping both and just finding something to wear underneath the top since I want to up the modesty of the dress.

title: Slimming, sexy, and chic
text:
How often do you see clothing that looks great on the model but looks lousy when you get it home? I thought for sure this crop top would look frumpy on me. I have a very good figure but I'm petite, and this is the type of top that looks best on a tall, lanky, lean model. Surprise, surprise! It actually made me look tall and lanky (but with a good bust, too!). I couldn't believe how nice it looked on me, and it had that purposely-blousy-chic look that everyone envies but no one actually achieves.
My tip is to disregard the size chart. The Small is supposed to fit a 27" bust, but it really doesn't. I'm a full 34B, and there was room to spare in the bust area. Keep in mind that there's no zipper to help you get this top on. It's all one piece. Apparently my hips are narrower than my shoulders, so I actually found it easier to clench my buttocks and slide the top up my legs than to tug it down over my shoulders. Just a tip for anyone who's broad-shouldered.
I ordered the black because it's meant to be worn braless and I didn't want the white to show anything indecent. It looks fantastic, and can be dressed up or down as much as you want. I love pairing it with jeans and black heels, big hoopy earrings, and big poofy hair.

text:

The construction is great, no flaws, well sewn, no weak spots that I can see, consistent quality throughout. I got these because I wanted a light summer type house boot. Something primarily for indoors, but something I won't ruin running out to the mailbox in. These work well for that purpose, and I love the design on the sides. I would round up if you are in between sizes, that worked well for me. These are not over large. I usually wear an 8 1/2 wide, I rounded up to 9, and these fit perfectly. Slightly shorter, but slightly wider than I am accustomed to a standard size 9 fitting me. These are not made narrow, but at the same time, they are not particularly roomy either. title: Solid, well built, concerned about money strap.
text:
I was worried this wallet would be too thick and hard to sit on considering it was aluminum, but that has not been the case. It is very comfortable in my pocket, no thicker than the last wallet that I have been using for over 10 years. There is plenty of room for cards and the wallet appears to be pretty well built.
My only issue has been with the money strap. The bills have a tendency to slip out when I pull the wallet from my pocket. This is not a design flaw necessarily, as the strap is tight and there is a small sticky rubber piece under the strap to help hold, but I will probably put my bills, especially the larger ones in the wallet instead of under the strap.
I do not have a way to test the RFID claims, but the aluminum should block attempts to scan RFID codes from cards.
Overall, this is a good wallet at a reasonable price.

title: Very compact
text:
This is a compact folding umbrella with a hardshell case. The case is in the shape of a tube, 8.5” long by 2.75” in diameter. It opens with a zipper and has a nylon strap loop on the end for hanging. The umbrella canopy is 38” in diameter when opened, the size of a standard umbrella, but the handle is just 18” long including the little plastic knob handle, so you have to hold your hand up by your chin when carrying this umbrella opened. The fabric for the canopy is a thin light-duty polyester, black on the inside and colored on the outside. The spines have plastic tips to hold the canopy.

I find this umbrella great for travel. It packs very easily into any bag. The hardshell case also prevents the umbrella from getting other objects wet if you have to pack it while damp. The umbrella is fully mechanical with no spring-loaded assist. So you have to extend the telescoping handle by hand. You also have to push against the tension of the spines to get the canopy up. Getting the canopy up without a spring assist takes some strength. I didn’t find it impossible, but I was able to do it without assistance. I had no problems folding the umbrella again or getting it back into the case. Yes, you need to use a little force to get the case to re-zip over the umbrella, but it’s a lot easier than trying to pack a tent or other large folded object into a small case. The only potential problem I can see with this umbrella is that the fabric is very light, so I don’t know how durable the canopy will be in the long run. Overall, this umbrella is a good choice when packing space is at a premium but you still need a full-sized umbrella.

title: It holds a LOT!
text:
I’m delighted with this bag! I’ve been following an Asian Beauty skincare routine, and I suddenly have way more bottles than I know what to do with! I bought a new shelf for the bathroom, but we’re planning a trip next week and I was a bit flummoxed about how to transport all my (expensive) face goodies. I saw this bag and thought maybe it would be perfect!

And guess what? I think it *almost* is! I’m really pleased with it! I can fit all my full size bottles in it. Even my dry shampoo fits fine. It’s got mesh pockets for my vials. I didn’t like the bags that turned half of your stuff upside down, I was worried that my products would leak. I love the side pockets- they will be great for makeup and likely my kid’s toothbrushes. The only thing I’ve noticed that it won’t hold is my electric toothbrush. I can fit it in if I lay it diagonally across the inside, but what would be the point of that?

The zippers all work and slide easily. There are no snags or loose threads for the zippers to get caught on. All the seams appear straight and complete. The color appears more or less as it did on my screen.

I’m really happy with the bag and think that I’ll use it for quite a while!

I was able to purchase this item at a discount in exchange for a thorough and honest review. All observations and comments are my own based on my use of this product. Please don't hesitate to leave your comments, ask questions, or push the “yes” button and tell me that this review was helpful!

title: Exceptional Construction, Reasonable Accuracy
text:
6/11/2022

Pagani Design
Red Black GMT Homage watch

I went searching for wrist watches on Amazon and stumbled on the Pagani Design brand. The offerings looked like a good deal; if their products were durable and accurate. I am highly dissatisfied with the Stauer brand after many years; the watches are not durable (both cosmetically and mechanically) and become inaccurate. I ordered the Red Black GMT Homage watch ($139.99). The black is more blue so it resembles Magnum's Rolex GMT Master II ($15,000+).

The watch was shipped from China and I received the package 9 days after order via the USPS. My first impression was that the packaging was super, the watch itself had thick plastic film covering the components to prevent scratching. The crown had a hefty weight and the bracelet was well designed and fabricated. Adjusting the bracelet to my scrawny wrist took a while but its not hard to figure out and if you have the right tools. I used some YouTube videos to get me started. The clasp release is impressive.

I tested the accuracy after a day of wearing it and it was about 10 seconds fast after 24 hours. This isn't bad since all I have to do is stop the watch every few days to have NIST time catch up. Which brings me to the time adjustment. Adjusting the time was easy but I couldn't get to the “fast” day adjustment and the GMT hand adjustment was hit or miss. I need to do more reading and research on these adjustments.

Based on the construction design, materials and quality I expect this jewel to last a long time, while keeping accurate time. I would buy another product in the future.

text: I really wanted to like these leggings. I wanted to love them. No, really. They are so soft, and felt super amazing. The outside is deliciously smooth, while the inside is like kittens hugging my legs. So, comfy leggings on, I sat down at the computer to read some news and rock out some homework. After only 2.5 hours of sitting almost entirely still. I'm terrified to even look at the other two pair that I ordered, much less try them on. With a heavy heart, I must return these and continue my search for clothes that can contain my booty for longer than 2 hours while keeping up with the overwhelming demands of my rather sedentary lifestyle. Two stars because the product would have been magical, if not for the remarkably short lifespan. First two photos are me being excited about new leggings! title: Both look very nice and I've worn them multiple times and gotten compliments ...
text:
I bought 2 of these ties: moss green and navy. Both look very nice and I've worn them multiple times and gotten compliments on them. Not too matte, not too shiny, just right. Good feel and good moderate texture. Thick but not overly bulky and they take a decent dimple. The moss green is a bit more like the color you would expect from the seller image (between a kelly green and a dark green, very distinguished and nice shade). The navy is obviously blue but very deep and rich. I like the shade quite a bit.

Now, all of that said, I wish the tie were a tad longer or the area you're supposed to have under your collar were a bit further towards the end of the back blade. I've found that I have to fiddle with the length and pull rather tightly to get a nice sized knot with an appropriate length on the front blade (I'm not particularly tall either at 5'-10" with a normally proportioned torso). Still, it's doable and I like it just fine. I just have to either have extra time to fidget with the length or pull my chinos higher than I would like (not quite grandpa territory, but edging in on it). Could be a problem with jeans that sit on your hips but I haven't worn either with jeans yet. I also wish the tag on the back blade were smaller or stitched down on the top and bottom of the tag so as to make undoing the tie a bit easier.

In short, buy these if you want to try out knit ties without much expense/risk. They will definitely look nice, wear well, and feel good and will certainly get you compliments. Just be aware that you will likely have to spend more time getting your look "right" for your torso and don't expect it to be a $50-100 tie and you'll be all set!

Easy remedy, though! I just got a pair of sew-in hook and eye fasteners like [[ASIN:B004BP7MIS Dritz Hooks & Eyes Nickel Size 2]], and sewed them into the outer waistline...the hook about 6 inches to the left of the front center waistline, and the eye about 6 inches to the right of the front center waistline. title: Top of the Line G-Shock
text:
I have owned quite a few G-Shocks over the past 15 years, and this is by far the most robust and elegant of them all. There are a few points of clarification that I would like to make, as the product description is somewhat misleading.

1.) This piece DOES NOT have a temperature gauge, barometric pressure gauge, or compass (contrary to the somewhat vague wording used in the description). It does have a moon phase depiction, tidal gauge, standard timer, stopwatch, alarms, "world" clock etc.
2.) This piece IS NOT made in the U.S.A. If one peeks at the reverse of the watch, they will note that it is made in Japan. This is also indicated on the reverse side of the metal buckle. Personally, I consider this to be a desirable trait when I purchase a G-Shock, as the quality and attention to detail are higher level when manufactured in Japan. This is my personal opinion, but for G-Shock connoisseurs, the differences are there, albeit subtle.

All in all, I am VERY impressed by the build quality, heft of the watch, and attention to detail by Casio on this G-Shock. With respect to this piece's lack of "atomic clock synchronization," I could care less personally. The only G-Shock I've owned with atomic clock synchronization gave up the ghost after a year and a half of light use and ample charging. These watches are fairly accurate pieces, and the number of "seconds" one may lose over the course of a year is negligible at best. I can think of very few applications where someone might need a piece continuously synched with the atomic clock each evening. Simply put, atomic synchronization, while "neat," is a bit of a gimmick.

With respect to wrist-size alluded to in some reviews, G-Shocks are meant to be large watches, regardless of the size of your wrist. I've always had small to average size wrists, and I enjoy the largest of the G-Shocks. Pick what you like with the features you like, and enjoy the piece!

Summary: high quality, solid build, fantastic attention to detail, worth the money.

title: Wonderful cleats. Thanks to Nike for continuing the line and still offering a leather boot.
text:
These fit my wide feet!

I've been on the hunt for new soccer cleats for several weeks. This is the 5th pair I've tried and the first pair which hasn't been too tight on my 100mm wide feet. The k-leather will stretch a little bit for a more custom fit, but the mesh on the inside should prevent them from stretching so much that they allow feet to slide around.

I usually wear a 9.5 cleat and 9.5 running shoe. These fit almost exact with a lightly padded sock. I'm going to need the leather to stretch just a bit to accommodate my big toe (height). There is zero extra room at the end of the shoe.

Material is very soft / supple, as k-leather should be. The heel liner is a suede-like material which is soft yet grippy. There is also some padding inside the heel to help with comfort and retention. I also find the lacing system helps pull your foot back and into the heel for retention. It's a noticeable difference between unlaced and tightly laced...locked down! I did get a blister on one heel the first time I used them, but that's to be expected with any new boot. They need to be broken in over the course of a few wears.

The sole plate is blue with some kind of iridescent chrome-like finish. It's flashy, but wears off. It appears the underlying color is still a translucent blue, so they'll still look good. White laces are going to get dirty and discolor. I happened to catch a review of these on youtube by SR4U and bought his light blue laces to go with the blue sole plate (laces are available on Amazon too).

Edit:
A month in and they are feeling wonderful. Broken in well. The leather is soft and supple. The "chrome" finish on the bottom is mostly gone and now just a blue sole plate. The fly knit sock portion in place of a normal tongue is no longer white. Playing on a couple of damp and rainy days it's now an off-white / brown color from a bit of dirt and mud. The white leather is also no longer pure white. Running and kicking has left some grass stains, though I haven't attempted to scrub them to see if it'll come out. Personally, I don't care. Cleats are never going to stay clean. The fit and comfort is worth it.
